Deified is a good game that should be quite appealing to people who like farming and turn based-strategy. I should start by saying I played "only" 10-ish hours for now but I think it should be the point where you understand fully the gameplay loop. Deified is basically a turn-based Hades, with a few twists to turn the real time skills needed in these kind of Rogue-lite games to more strategic skills. Your main character is equiped with one relic (a weapon of sorts) and needs to move through three floors made up of twenty to thirty chambers each and a boss you must defeat to gain permanent increases and ressources. Each chamber can either grant you the ability to purchase relics and then fight to gain ressources, or have some kind of special event like a healing fountain, a wandering merchant selling you rare stuff, a forge to add bonuses or remove the penalties to your relics and more... Throughout the chambers, your character will level up and each level will unlock him one additional relic (=weapon) slot for this run (up to 10). Each of these slot comes up with a bonus passive effect (i.e. killing an ennemy gives more gold, hitting an ennemy applies damage over time effects or even using the relic allowing you to use again another relic you already used this turn...) but also a penalty (i.e. the relic can only be used first/last each turn, the relic slot is deactivated if the relic is not of a specific rarity or has a specific range). All of this makes building very interesting : you have to think about which chambers you want to through to get relics, bonus or healing and you have to adapt your relics to the constraints you have while still trying to get good synergies overall. So if you are like me and use a common (=lowest grade) relic that gives you a shield as your only common relic and you get a relic slot that can only activate if you have a common relic inside it but also apply DoTs to ennemies hit, would you just equip the shield but not use the DoT bonus as the relic doesn't do damage ? Or try to buy and use another common relic in this slot ? Or maybe try to find a forge to remove the negative effect ? All of this makes each one of your runs unique and forces you to think about all your choices. Obviously as every Rogue-lite, you have some sort of meta progression that allows you to unlock permanent bonuses for you to go farther in your runs and be more flexible as your attempts increase. That's it for the gameplay which is for me the biggest reason to play this game. However the graphics part is still nice for a small indie studio and the music is also great, giving you this kind of mystery feeling that fits really well with the game's atmosphere. Overall I would say Deified is a solid indie game, even in it's early access form, that allows for some nice creativity in it's strategy. I am 11 hours in and just wrapped up my 3rd complete run, I have unlocked about a third of the meta progression and explored only 10-ish builds but I can easily see myself play for 20-30 more hours.

This is a small but very worthy project. A rare find in the turn-based combat category. At first, I was surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews, but after playing for 10 hours, I was pleasantly surprised myself. Pros: +Amazing meta-progression +Balance +Build variety +Difficulty +Refreshing features for the genre +Unique and fun to play Cons: -Secondary storyline and music -Few mods and complications, but maybe they'll add them after leaving EA -A few small bugs, but forgivable at this stage (considering the volume of mechanics) The project is somewhat reminiscent of Griftlands. It feels fresh and makes the gameplay enjoyable. It would be great if the project expanded in content and developed further in the future, but even at this stage, I can confidently recommend it to roguelike fans. It's difficult to estimate the content length yet, but I'd estimate it's around 30-40 hours

[b]TL;DR:[/b] The game has a very niche gameplay style, but if you enjoy tactical roguelikes (like Mewgenics, for example) you can go in blind! There are just a few interface issues and the occasional small bug, but that’s what Early Access is for, especially since they’re honestly very minor. [list] [hr][/hr] [h2]ART DIRECTION[/h2] [*][b][u]Sound Design & Music +++++[/u] : Probably one of the most immersive tactical roguelikes I’ve ever played. [*][b][u]Art ++++[/u] : Really beautiful, with some very interesting and bold designs. The atmosphere is very well conveyed. [*][b][u]Lore +++[/u] : The atmosphere is a bit mysterious, which is something rarely explored in this type of game. But the little bits of information you get during each run are enough to keep the spark of discovery alive! I can’t wait to learn more about the world as I keep playing! [*][b][u]Readability --[/u] : Some environments lack a bit of contrast, and/or have enemy models that look a little too similar. (Empusa 👀) [hr][/hr] [h2]GAMEPLAY[/h2] [*][b][u]Combat +++++[/u] : A very classic tactical system in the best way possible. There are plenty of QoL features that make planning easier. It’s simple, effective, smooth, and free of unnecessary clutter. Really clean! The sound design and visual effects do a great job of making attacks feel brutal at the right moments, which is very satisfying. [*][b][u]Relics +++++[/u] : The relic system and relic slot system are really well designed! Obviously, some builds are easier to set up than others, but all of them have a real way to win a run. On top of that, the game already offers a lot of flexibility, allowing you to adapt while still letting you “force” a build a little when you want to. [*][b][u]Enemies +++/--[/u] : I’m a bit more mixed on this aspect. The floor bosses all have a very clear identity, with very different strategies, and that’s an absolute JOY, especially since they can force you to adapt your build, otherwise they might just kill your run. The same goes for regular enemies: each one has a clear identity, with well-defined strengths and weaknesses.BUT I’m a little worried that having only one ability per enemy might make runs feel somewhat monotonous in the long run. [hr][/hr] [h2]REPLAYABILITY[/h2] [*][b][u]Meta Progression ++++/-[/u] : The game is well balanced enough that you can win without relying on meta progression. In fact, meta progression mostly makes your runs easier, but it’s not required to have fun. That said, I didn’t really feel like the game became harder as runs progressed, so as your meta progression advances, the game becomes easier and easier. Maybe a gradual difficulty increase over multiple runs would be nice, so you can enjoy the meta progression without eventually steamrolling the game. [*][b][u]Run Randomness +++[/u] : The game’s biggest strength is the relic slot system when leveling up! The fact that there are usage constraints can REALLY shape the direction of your run. And yet, it won’t necessarily kill your run either. The game gives you ways to compensate for “bad luck” when you have a build in mind, you just need to think things through until you find the right event. For those worried about the randomness of shops: yes, there is some variance, but nothing that will prevent you from enjoying the game. Overall, it feels well balanced ! [/list] [hr][/hr] [h2]SUMMARY[/h2] Overall, this is a little gem that isn’t fully polished yet, but is already completely playable and addictive enough to make you lose dozens of hours. If you enjoy this kind of game, don’t hesitate ; you won’t regret it.

Very competent tactical Roguelite. Combat is fun and with the different upgrades engaging enough to keep you going run after run. It is quite difficult which is something I appreciate (I'm not an expert in tactics games but I play a lot of roguelikes) BUT - only a handful of upgrades are interesting/meaningful enough to consider investing in, and the meta progression as of right now is VERY slow (which, to be fair, is mostly the reason why the game feels hard.) Some constructive criticism/ What I would personally like: - More enemy variety and more visual clarity on what they can do (A tooltip is "ok", but I feel like I shouldn't have to click on the boss and hover on his attack to read his peculiarity - for example, the [spoiler] Twin [/spoiler] or [spoiler] The Star [/spoiler] are great, because visually you can understand their gimmick and are somewhat simple to get. Others, not so much. - Either a lot of small upgrades with easy-to-get points (So you can immediately go in a run and feel the difference of the +5% dmg you got), or few, big meaningful upgrades with slow progression. - Maybe starting "classes" for the protagonist? Like, just a simple passive that you can choose before starting a run, so the same combination of relics doesn't play exactly the same between runs, by interacting with the passive (ex: Mage class, each turn you don't cast an ability it gets 25% effectivness, or a warrior class who's passive gives +1 to any dmg dealt in a 1 sq. radius. - In the same spirit, run-specific modifiers are a must in these types of games, especially in the form of devil deals. +50 effectivness to the leftmost relic BUT the rightmost is locked, for example. The system where whenever you level up you unlock a slot with already a positive and negative modifier is "okay", but loses value when most of the time you can just rush to a blacksmith (IMHO, I feel like some people could easily disagree with this one). - Bugfixes. Right now, there are quite a few, very annoying and run ending bugs. I don't wanna underline this point because I really like the game, but if it was mediocre this would be a dealbreaker for me. That said, I really enjoyed my time with this game and I would love to pick it up again in the future, maybe even wipe my file and start over. Good stuff.

It has good gameplay and strategy but the rogue-LITE aspects kinda kill it for me, because it takes the skill aspect from the game. Its basically like you are supposed to die and grind to be able to beat the game over time when you have the upgrades unlocked, which is disappointing because at that point you aren't playing the mechanics, you are arbitrarily grinding. A fix would be at least not to be able to unlock ALL of the skills available, and only be able to equip a select number of skills or something to where its like build oritented or something, but I know that won't happen. But this is a problem with all rogue-LITE games, and of these games, this one is basically the best. Turn this game into a rogue-LIKE, only skill and RNG with no overlap between runs and it would be a 10/10.

Very good game with a real focus on synergies and combos. I got hooked up in the first 10 minutes and now I just want to play it again and again to test every synergy. The game design is quite good, with numerous playstyles and enemy variations. I enjoy the artistic direction, with drawn 2D sprites and UI ; though the 3D animations might still need development to match the smooth 2D style. I also love the fact that the early access is getting many updates for balancing, you see problems being fixed quickly. (PS : there is a boss room on the 2nd floor with many crevices that you can fall in, even if there are walls in front of them, so the feedback is a bit messy and I got screwed many times, losing a game because I fell even though I couldn't see it coming ;))

Deified is a great roguelite game, the number of builds you can make and all the mechanics work great together to give you a rush of dopamine in every run. The game has some performance issues, particularly later in the game when there's a lot of blood on the ground, where the fps will drop a lot. It has some UI bugs as well but nothing serious, the game never crashed on me. Overall, I think Deified is worth the money. Hopefully with full release, the performance issues are fixed.

[h1]One More Run... Every Time[/h1] This is one of those games that quietly hooks you. I bought it expecting to play for an hour or two, and suddenly I'm dozens of runs in saying, "just one more." [hr][/hr] [h2]What It Does Well[/h2] [list] [*]Excellent progression that keeps every run meaningful. [*]Tons of build variety without becoming overwhelming. [*]Unlocks constantly give you something new to experiment with. [*]Runs are fast enough that failure never feels punishing. [*]The gameplay loop is incredibly addictive. [/list] [h2]The Best Part[/h2] The game constantly makes you think. Do you play safe or get greedy? Do you invest in long-term power or survive the next encounter? Every decision feels important, and when a build finally comes together it is incredibly satisfying. [h2]Difficulty[/h2] The difficulty feels fair. Most losses were because I got too ambitious or tried a new strategy rather than because the game felt unfair. Even after winning, there are additional progression systems and challenges that make you want to keep playing. [h2]A Couple Small Suggestions[/h2] [list] [*]I'd love a little more transparency around some of the progression systems. [*]A few unlock requirements could be explained a bit better. [*]add a better codex for what buffs/debuffs, and mechanism transparency [/list] [h2]Final Thoughts[/h2] If you enjoy games like Slay the Spire, Shogun Showdown, Monster Train, Balatro, or other roguelite deck/build games, this is absolutely worth your time. It's polished, addictive, and has that rare quality where every run teaches you something new. [b]Easy recommendation. Highly recommended.[/b]
It's quite a nice game, even while still in early access. Looking forward to see how it gets better
